Partly as a result of this review, Kalamazoo and Macon will have console compactors, and St. Louis will have under-the-counter compactors and a satellite collection vehicle. These installations will have special evaluations made of their usefulness, cost and efficiency.
In addition, the Environmental Protection Agency will conduct, through a contractor, a continuing evaluation of the solid waste management activities on all prototype sites.
e) <u>Recreation</u>: Careful attention has also been given to the recreational potential of all of the sites. Each of the site designs provides community facilities, (all but two including swimming pools) with open play areas and smaller "tot lots" in areas under direct supervision from the housing units.
Existing or planned city or county parks plan an important part in the planning of the Indianapolis, Kalamazoo, Memphis, King County, St. Louis and Seattle sites. In Indianapolis, ten acres of the prototype site area was dedicated to the city, which is developing a park to serve the site and the neighborhood; prior to this, the nearest open space to the site was one and one-half miles away. The Kalamazoo site was a relatively unused portion of an existing city park; the site design has kept the ridge line overlooking the lake-side area free from housing units, preserving the slope for park use. Also in Kalamazoo, HUD arranged an open space grant for the city to assist in providing major park facilities in another portion of the city which lacked such amenities. In Memphis, a small park area is being developed by the program to be dedicated to the city. In St. Louis, the West site provides space for a city park adjacent to the housing area. In Seattle, the site will be abutted on three sides by a new city park, and conceptual design for this park has been coordinated with the BREAKTHROUGH design.
The King County site is adjacent to a utility line right-of-way, and the site planner, working with county officials, developed a plan to use this eighty-foot-wide easement in a planned county trail network and recreation area. the county is planning to develop land to the North of this easement for additional park purposes.
f) Educational Facilities: The impact of the BREAKTHROUGH site on local school capacities was important on the Jersey City site. A supplemental school will be constructed as part of the site development and leased to the school department in Jersey City.
g) Transportation and Parking: Site planning has taken the availability of existing public transportation into consideration at every site; as an example, arrangements have been made for local busses to stop at the Kalamazoo community center. Four of the sites are in central city urban renewal areas, and parking has been of particular concern at these sites.
